I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to protect yield in dry periods, but because I am 70 years old and my household labor is limited, I will keep management practical and not make it too complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on moderate fertilizer, irrigate at key stages, and use rotary tillage because it is manageable and fits how I prepare land after maize. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep fertilizer a bit higher on nitrogen, reduce tillage to no-tillage after wheat to save time and labor, and irrigate when the crop most needs water. I will also keep pesticide use limited to what I think is necessary, because I want to control pests and disease without doing more sprays than needed.
